author: conductor
title: Agent templates declare BOTH MCP tool prefixes plus ToolSearch — launcher-mode-agnostic, no baked variable
statement:
Every `agent-templates/*.md` `tools:` line declares, for each Sterling store tool, BOTH mounted names — `mcp__sterling__<tool>` AND `mcp__plugin_sterling_sterling__<tool>` — and additionally lists `ToolSearch`. Rationale in one line: the correct prefix is a function of the LAUNCHER, not of the install, and Sterling generates both launchers for the same project, so no single value baked at install time can be right.

Grounding (research_finding 34a03611, CC 2.1.220, live subagent probes): `--plugin-dir` alone mounts ONLY `mcp__plugin_sterling_sterling__*`; `--mcp-config … --strict-mcp-config` (sterling-windows.bat) mounts ONLY `mcp__sterling__*` because `--strict` suppresses the plugin manifest's server. Listing both is accepted in either mode — the unmounted name is ignored, the mounted one is granted, no error.

`ToolSearch` is the mode-INDEPENDENT half of the fix and the actual root cause of the reported failure: Sterling MCP tools are served DEFERRED to subagents in both modes, so an agent with the right prefix but no `ToolSearch` cannot call the store at all (probe: `CALLABLE=NO`). Every agent therefore carries it.

This supersedes in effect the single-prefix mandate of decision 097851ed (`mcp__plugin_sterling_sterling__*`), whose text lives in the dev-machine store and was unreadable from this machine; 097851ed was not wrong, it was mode-incomplete — correct for plugin mode, silently dead under the strict-mcp launcher. Supersede it explicitly from a dev-machine session.

Verified after the fix: the real `explorer` agent returns STORE=REACHABLE in BOTH launcher modes; `npm run check` clean; 508-test suite green.

alternatives_rejected.option: Hard-flip every template to `mcp__sterling__*` (the TODO's proposed step 1)
alternatives_rejected.reason: Fixes the strict-mcp launcher and SILENTLY BREAKS the WSL/plugin launcher, which this repo also generates — verified: `mcp__sterling__*` is ABSENT under `--plugin-dir` alone. Trades one silent failure for another, and the failure mode (agents simply lack tools, no error) is exactly what made the original defect survive a full day of SpaceExplorer runs.

alternatives_rejected.option: A `{{MCP_PREFIX}}` substitution token resolved at install/sync time (the TODO's proposed step 2)
alternatives_rejected.reason: The existing vars machinery in agent-distribution.mjs would support it, but there is no correct value to bake: init generates BOTH sterling.bat (WSL/plugin) and sterling-windows.bat (native/strict) for the same project, so the prefix depends on which launcher the user double-clicks — a runtime fact, not an install-time one. Would need a recorded canonical launcher mode plus a sync-agents re-bake on every mode flip, and is silently wrong in the interim. Strictly more machinery for strictly less coverage than listing both.

alternatives_rejected.option: Drop `--strict-mcp-config` from sterling-windows.bat so the plugin server mounts in both launchers, leaving one true prefix
alternatives_rejected.reason: Attacks the right seam but changes how and where the MCP server RUNS on native Windows — out of scope for a template fix, and `--strict` was added deliberately to stop native claude inheriting the WSL-node plugin server. Would need its own verification that the plugin manifest's Windows-node config serves the native session correctly. Left as an available future simplification, not taken as a drive-by.

alternatives_rejected.option: Add ToolSearch only, keep the single plugin prefix
alternatives_rejected.reason: ToolSearch alone fixes the WSL launcher but leaves every strict-mcp session (including sterling-main's own native launcher and SpaceExplorer's) with zero store tools. Half a fix for a defect whose whole character is silence.

rationale: Triggered by TODO-agent-tool-prefix.md, carried from a SpaceExplorer session (2026-07-20) where every coder/test-writer spawn reported 'knowledge tools absent' and a librarian agent exited `blocked` on first dispatch. The TODO diagnosed the prefix as simply wrong; probing showed it is mode-dependent and that the missing `ToolSearch` — not the prefix — is the mode-independent root cause. P5 (fail loud) is imperfectly served here: the platform ignores an unmounted tool name silently, so dual-declaration buys correctness rather than loudness; the compensating control is that the store is now reachable in every mode, so there is no silent-failure state left to detect. P3 favors the zero-machinery option: no new token, no new config field, no new resolution path that can itself drift.
